featured_reviews.name: Raghuspeaks
featured_reviews.review_text:
Vietnam Trip Debrief: The Highs, the Lows, and the Unsung Hero

​Overall, this trip managed to hit a 5-star high, but that victory was hard earned against some serious turbulence. Here is the breakdown of what made the trip spectacular, and where things went entirely off script.

The Highs: Absolute Wins

​The Ultimate MVP (Tour Manager Megha Shinde): We struck absolute gold with Megha. She was the heartbeat of the tour, effortless and vibrant. She kept the group atmosphere lighthearted, and genuinely fun. Without her, this trip would have been a 3 star affair; she single-handedly elevated it to a 5-star masterpiece.

​The food across the board was phenomenal. Every single meal was a delicious highlight. Frequent Travellers will agree food in most foreign trip is deeply ignored.

​The hotel accommodations were fantastic. Clean spacious rooms welcomed us which is again a rare win for any traveler.

​The local guides, Khan, Micheal and Charlie were fantastic. They were not pushy like most local guides were have dealt in the past.

Our group though a bit noisy were incredibly disciplined, respecting schedules.

The Lows :  The Villain

​VietJet takes the crown for the absolute worst airline experience to date. The check-in counter staff were downright hostile.

Our trip started with a bad note with the airline putting my family of 3 in different corners of the aircraft, forcing us to pay extra just to sit together. This was a massive oversight on Veena World’s logistical planning.

​The local hospitality left much to be desired. The local attitude was surprisingly cold, rude and at times arrogant.

They hate the chinese but behaved like one (people who dealt with the Chinese will understand) exposing a racist and unfriendly demeanor.

On Day 1 Forcing sight-seeing immediately upon arrival before hotel check-in is a grueling design. Veena World needs to negotiate early check-ins so weary travelers can freshen up before hitting the streets.

Itenary on Departure Day also should be kept light.
We got incredibly lucky that the weather held out for our excursion to the Cu Chi Tunnels (something  I was looking forward being a history buff) which turned out to be an absolutely mind-blowing experience

A sudden downpour would have ruined it. Hence, the final day needs to be kept light and breezy.

To summarise ,
While most Lows need Vietnamese people to fix, if they want to truly flourish as a top-tier tourist destination, the logistical hiccups are entirely within Veena World's power to correct for future travelers.

​Ultimately, despite the flaws and airline headaches, Megha saved the day, turning potential disasters into a truly memorable vacation. If it was not for her, the smiles on the group would have been missing.
